purpose: Qualitative demand/friction intelligence for the single Stödassistenten learning system. Scores are prioritization signals, not measured search volumes and not proof of legal right, a specific school measure, diagnosis, appeal outcome or individual decision. Natural-language pages and community-facing material are discovery signals; school-support facts require current primary-source verification.

scoring.priority_rule: Prioritize combinations of high demand, high friction, high consequence and weak current product coverage. Scores are qualitative prioritization, not measured search volumes.

demand_signal.basis: The same practical questions recur across parent-facing material: whether diagnosis is needed, what the school should do when reading/writing or concentration difficulties persist, and where to go when meetings or existing adjustments do not resolve the problem. This is qualitative discovery, not measured search volume.

friction_signal.basis: Users can easily conflate diagnosis, extra adjustments, special-support investigation, action programmes, school health involvement, principal responsibility and appeal. The current public family journey offered a school choice but then returned the same generic family-benefit rows regardless of that choice.

miss_consequence.basis: A false diagnosis gate can delay school support, while overpromising a particular measure or appeal outcome can mislead a family about rights and next steps during an already consequential school difficulty.

source_fragmentation.basis: Skolverket separates general support rules, easy-language parent guidance and organisational guidance, while formal action-programme appeals are handled by Skolväsendets överklagandenämnd.

language_accessibility_friction.basis: Terms such as extra anpassningar, särskilt stöd, utredning, elevhälsa and åtgärdsprogram are process-heavy even in Swedish. Families starting from a concrete problem rather than legal vocabulary face additional friction in Arabic or Persian.

steps_to_action.basis: A safe route can be shortened to child age plus one high-information question about what the school has already done, then branch to teacher/principal clarification, prompt special-support investigation, or the official appeal path when a formal decision exists.

recurrence_signal.basis: Recurring misunderstandings include believing diagnosis is required, assuming diagnosis guarantees a particular intervention, waiting for healthcare before school action, and not knowing the difference between informal dissatisfaction and a formal appealable action-programme decision.

current_product_coverage_gap.basis: The canonical scenario lab already contained child ADHD and reading/writing school-support benchmarks and the root shell could route broad family school-support language, but person-pilot's family result list stayed generic and did not use Skolverket or a school-state question to change the next action.

signals.recommended_learning_action: Keep one product and one person module. Turn the existing child school-support benchmark into an executable same-shell route: do not ask diagnosis as a gate, ask only what the school has already done after the child age guard, then select the source-grounded next action. Keep any normalized legal/process fields review-gated and retain structured anonymous feedback without raw child, school or health text.
signals.truth_rule: Discovery language and qualitative scores are never truth. Verify diagnosis boundaries, extra-adjustment rules, special-support investigation, principal responsibility and appealable decisions against current Skolverket and Skolväsendets överklagandenämnd primary sources. Never infer a diagnosis, guaranteed measure or appeal outcome from user text, feedback, a prior AI answer or discovery material.
